name: – Pierre Pimpie – Motion for a resolution (as a whole)
title: REPORT on the implementation of the VAT reverse-charge mechanism
part_text:
The report is Parliament's opinion, not a new law. It asks to keep the EU's "reverse charge" VAT rule, which makes the buyer rather than the seller pay VAT on risky goods like phones, metals and energy, past its current end date of 31 December 2026. It wants a longer extension, clearer shared rules across countries, a simpler emergency procedure, and checks every two years.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament asks to extend the rule and tidy it up.
- **Who it affects:** Businesses trading in high-risk goods, especially small firms, and national tax offices.
- **What happens next:** The Commission and Member States decide; the Commission must assess the rule and report.
